digest:
DATASET: Supplement Impact — 1000 synthetic participants on sports-nutrition regimens.
Columns: Age (18-65), Gender (Male/Female/Non-Binary), Supplement (Creatine Monohydrate / Mass Gainer / Both),
Weeks (4-24 cycle length), Initial_WT & Final_WT (kg), Strength_Gain (% increase), Primary_Benefit (self-report).
Derived: WT_Change = Final_WT - Initial_WT (kg). Data is clean: no missing values, no duplicate IDs,
every participant gained weight. Overall mean strength gain = 16.4% (range 5-30%).

STRENGTH GAIN BY SUPPLEMENT (CoV = coefficient of variation; lower = more consistent):
  - Both: n=344, mean strength gain=22.59%, std=4.59, CoV=20.3% (consistency), weight change=8.04kg
  - Creatine Monohydrate: n=317, mean strength gain=18.22%, std=4.74, CoV=26.0% (consistency), weight change=1.47kg
  - Mass Gainer: n=339, mean strength gain=8.35%, std=2.32, CoV=27.9% (consistency), weight change=6.53kg
Highest average: Both. Most consistent (lowest CoV): Both.

WEIGHT vs STRENGTH SPLIT: Mass Gainer drives weight (~6.53kg) but
little strength; Creatine drives strength with almost no weight change
(~1.47kg); 'Both' leads on both axes.

STRENGTH GAIN BY GENDER (flat — gender is randomly assigned noise):
  - Female: 16.03%
  - Male: 16.2%
  - Non-Binary: 16.87%

CORRELATIONS with Strength_Gain (all near zero — demographics barely matter):
  - Age: 0.029
  - Weeks: 0.07
  - Initial_WT: -0.002
  - WT_Change: 0.008

STRENGTH GAIN BY PRIMARY_BENEFIT (all ~16%, so the self-reported benefit does NOT predict strength):
  - Strength Gain: n=208, mean strength=16.52%
  - Cognitive Support: n=209, mean strength=16.47%
  - Weight Gain: n=210, mean strength=16.38%
  - Muscle Recovery: n=172, mean strength=16.37%
  - Bone Density: n=201, mean strength=16.14%

PREDICTIVE MODEL (target = Strength_Gain %, predictors = Age, Weeks, Initial_WT, Gender, Supplement;
Final_WT and Primary_Benefit excluded as post-cycle leakage; 5-fold cross-validation):
  - Baseline (mean): MAE=6.33pp, R2=-0.001
  - Linear Regression: MAE=3.39pp, R2=0.684
  - Random Forest: MAE=3.5pp, R2=0.648
  - Gradient Boosting: MAE=3.46pp, R2=0.669
Best model: Linear Regression (MAE 3.39 percentage points, R2 0.684).
Permutation importance (drop in R2 when a feature is shuffled):
  - Supplement: 1.364
  - Weeks: 0.002
  - Age: 0.001
  - Initial_WT: 0.0
  - Gender: 0.0
TAKEAWAY: Supplement choice is essentially the ONLY driver of strength gain; Age, Gender, Weeks and
starting weight add almost nothing. The R2 ceiling (~0.684) reflects that within-supplement spread
is mostly irreducible random noise in this synthetic data.
